title: Target gap pairs
statement: A sorted list contains distinct integer reading levels from 0 to 100. Count pairs of positions i < j whose later level minus earlier level is exactly 3. Return the count. The list may be empty and has at most 100 entries; do not change it.

lesson.summary: Keep two increasing indices. If the difference is below three advance right; if above three advance left. On an exact match count one and advance both; keep left strictly below right.
recognition: The input is sorted and levels are distinct.
Moving either boundary changes the difference predictably.
Keep left, right and a match count.
lesson.invariant: Every discarded left level is exhausted or paired; every discarded right level cannot form an uncounted gap-three pair with an earlier surviving left. The pointers only advance.
lesson.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
pitfalls: Allowing left to equal right admits an invalid self-pair.
Using two pointers without sorted input invalidates the monotonic argument.
Distinct input is required by this exact counting algorithm.

review.prompt: The current gap is below three. Why is advancing only the right pointer safe?

options.text: Advancing left increases the difference and preserves every possible match.
For this left level, every right level up to the current one has a gap below three; a later right level may reach three.
Advancing both pointers is always safe because the levels are distinct.

review.rationale: Sortedness makes all earlier right levels too close to the current left level. Keeping left and advancing right preserves a possible later match; moving both can skip it.

transfer.title: Pairs around a target sum
transfer.statement: In a sorted distinct list, count pairs summing to 10. Explain why one pointer now starts at the opposite end and moves inward.
transfer.invariant: Discarded endpoint pairs cannot reach the target under sortedness; each match uses two distinct positions.
transfer.expectedReasoning: Increase the left endpoint when the sum is too small and decrease the right endpoint when too large. A difference-based same-direction trace cannot be reused unchanged.
